short_title: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? 🛁 #shorts
short_description:
Those wrinkly bath fingers aren't just soggy skin. After about five minutes in warm water, your nervous system makes the blood vessels in your fingertips narrow, the pads lose volume, and the skin folds into wrinkles. The proof: when the nerve to a finger is damaged, that finger stays smooth, which is why doctors have used water immersion as a simple nerve test.

Why would we have this reflex? A 2013 study (Biology Letters) found that wrinkled fingers handle wet objects better, like treads on a tire. A 2014 study (PLOS ONE) couldn't confirm it, so scientists still debate it.
